title: Enterprise intake rubric for streaming + tool-chain requests with structured-schema readiness
creator: Priya Singh
description: Create a repeatable intake and prioritization rubric specifically for enterprise feature requests that combine streaming chat, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. The goal is to accelerate decisioning for requests that have cross-cutting requirements (SLA, security, data residency, observability, and model compatibility) and produce a clear path: quick-decision, staged delivery (MVS -> Beta -> GA), and an engineering handoff checklist.
background: We continue to receive high-touch enterprise asks that bundle streaming chat, multi-step toolchains, and strict structured output schemas. Current triage is ad-hoc: PMs and SEs manually coordinate with infra/eng/security which increases lead time and causes mis-scoped engagements. This ticket captures a proposed rubric and gating checklist to be used by intake owners and Solutions Engineering.
proposed_triage_rubric: Customer commitment: contract value, active pilots, and timeline urgency (Low/Medium/High)
SLA & availability needs: required p99 latency, throughput, and uptime targets
Privacy & compliance: data residency, logging retention, and required certifications (SOC2/ISO/GDPR entitlements)
Security surface: plaintext vs encrypted payloads, KMS/HSM integration, SSO/SAML and audit logging needs
Model compatibility: required model families, quantization/precision constraints, and deterministic output expectations
Structured schema enforcement: strict schema validation, additional sanitizer/transformation steps, and contract testing needs
Streaming characteristics: single vs multi-turn streaming, maximum simultaneous streams per tenant, and early-close semantics
Tool/function complexity: number of external tool integrations, stateful tool-chains, authorization boundaries
Operational cost impact: expected tokens/hour, KV cache hit expectations, and estimated incremental GPU-hours
Observability requirements: per-route tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and SLA alert thresholds
Rollback/fallback plan: compatible fallback model or degraded capability to meet availability
gating_checklist: Legal/Contract sign-off or confirmed commercial interest
Security review required: threat model and data flow approved
Network/VPC design for Private or Dedicated options if requested
Telemetry hooks defined: traces, request/response samples (scrubbed), and cost tagging
Performance baseline: latency/throughput targets and a plan for load testing
Schema contract tests added to CI and example golden payloads provided
Canary rollout plan with automatic fallback to hosted-compatible model
Support & on-call escalation documented for Beta and GA
acceptance_criteria: Intake rubric documented and published to Confluence
Triage checklist added to PM intake playbook and intake form updated
Solutions Engineering has a one-pager for customer-facing expectation setting
Two pilot requests triaged with rubric and results captured (lessons learned)
One ENG ticket template created for handoffs that includes gating checklist
initial_assessment_notes: Example: Major retail customer requests low-latency streaming chat + payment toolchain with strict purchase JSON schema and 13-region data residency. Initial ask: pilot in 8 weeks.
Risk observed: schema validation failure modes could cause data loss if not canonicalized; fallback behavior must be explicit
Engineering rough estimate: 3 sprints for MVS + infra config if Dedicated/VPC required
Suggested immediate outcome: classify as 'High' customer commitment and schedule 1:1 discovery with Solutions Engineering and Security
